agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: Agent-relevant as a pip-installable CLI and Python package with a documented one-shot invocation ('vibe-trading run -p "..."') and a swarm mode, so an orchestrating agent can drive it as a subprocess and consume the run cards it emits. hlido_opinion.headline: An open-source finance research agent that draws its own boundary at execution — the most carefully scoped trading-adjacent agent we have seen, and unverified by our checks.
hlido_opinion.body: Hlido's automated public-surface checks recorded no passes on this run even though the page rendered and was captured in full, so the score reflects what our checks could VERIFY, not a judgement that the product is weak. Read the score as low confidence pending a re-test, and the notes below as what the captured surface says about itself. Vibe-Trading turns natural-language market questions into runnable research, and the thing that distinguishes it from the crowded 'AI trading bot' category is a boundary section that limits the product rather than expanding it. The captured page states it is built for research, simulation and backtesting; that any live trading is opt-in and read-only by default; that it runs only through a broker the user authorises, within limits the user sets, and can be halted instantly; that it holds no funds and operates no execution venue; and that it is not investment advice and is experimental. In a category where overclaiming is the norm and the downside is a user's money, a vendor that writes down what it will not do is giving a reader something far more useful than a performance figure. The capability surface is specific: eleven backtesting engines across A-shares, global, Indian, Korean and Vietnamese equities, crypto, futures, forex, cross-market composites and options portfolios; preset swarm teams (investment committee, quant desk, risk review, macro, crypto); a 'shadow account' that parses broker journals, extracts implicit rules and runs counterfactual backtests; and an agent harness with persistent memory, session search, editable skills and context compression. A documented four-stage loop (route, ground, test, deliver) returns run cards, tool traces and caveats, which is the right shape for research you may need to defend later. Two cautions. The illustrative CLI output on the page shows a +18.6% return with -7.4% max drawdown — a marketing example, not a result, and a reader could easily take it for one. And the claimed 37.2k stars and 6.7K monthly installs are self-reported.

tier_rationale: FADING (50) is a measurement verdict: all required public-surface checks failed on this run, so the engine count, the harness features and the self-reported adoption figures are unconfirmed by us. In a domain where a wrong answer costs a user money, an unverified claim must not earn a tier — a re-test is queued. It is not lower because the captured surface is unusually disciplined: it states its own limits, disclaims investment advice, and makes the execution boundary explicit rather than burying it.
what_it_does_well: Draws an explicit boundary at execution: research and backtesting only, live trading opt-in and read-only by default
States plainly that it holds no funds, runs no execution venue, and is not investment advice
Broker authorisation stays with the user, within user-set limits, with an instant halt
Backtesting breadth is enumerated by market rather than claimed generically (eleven engines, named markets)
The research loop (route, ground, test, deliver) returns run cards, tool traces and caveats — defensible output
Shadow-account counterfactual backtesting against real broker journals is a genuinely differentiated capability
Labels itself experimental rather than production-ready
what_it_fails_at: All required public-surface checks failed on this run — none of the capability claims is independently verified by us
The illustrative CLI output (+18.6% return, -7.4% max drawdown) reads like a result and is not one
No published backtest methodology, so look-ahead and survivorship-bias handling is unknown
Self-reported adoption figures (37.2k stars, 6.7K installs/mo) with no method
Eleven backtesting engines across many markets is a large surface with no per-engine validation evidence
Financial-domain software with no stated audit, compliance posture or data-provenance detail
best_for: Quantitative researchers who want natural-language access to backtesting across multiple markets
Agent-driven research pipelines where reproducible run artifacts matter
Analysts reviewing their own broker journals for implicit rules and counterfactuals
Non-US market coverage (A-shares, Indian, Korean, Vietnamese equities) that most tools skip
not_recommended_for: Anyone seeking automated live trading — the project explicitly declines that role
Users expecting investment advice or validated strategy performance
Regulated institutions needing an audited, compliant research platform
Anyone who would read the illustrative return figure as evidence of performance
red_flags: An illustrative CLI output showing '+18.6%' return and '-7.4% max drawdown' sits on the public surface where a reader can mistake a demo string for a measured result
No published backtesting methodology — look-ahead and survivorship-bias handling is unknown, which is the first question any backtest claim must answer
All required public-surface checks failed on this run while the page rendered fully — the score reflects unverified claims, not measured weakness; a re-test is queued

compared_to.verdict_diff: Open Interpreter is a general local code-execution agent you could point at market data yourself. Vibe-Trading ships the finance domain — eleven backtest engines, preset research teams, broker-journal parsing — plus an explicit execution boundary. General tool versus domain tool.

CrewAI is the framework for assembling the kind of multi-agent research team Vibe-Trading ships pre-built (investment committee, quant desk, risk review). Build it with CrewAI if your process is unusual; take the presets if it is not.
